relations.definition: To be in a romantic relationship with someone and plan to marry them.
relations.embedding_query_text: isEngagedTo: To be in a romantic relationship with someone and plan to marry them.

chosen_property.label: isEngagedTo
chosen_property.definition: To be in a romantic relationship with someone and plan to marry them.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits this relation.

candidates.label: spouse
candidates.comment: A marital relation between two persons who are married to each other. Also called "husband", "wife", "married to", "partner". Examples: "John has spouse Jane", "Mary's spouse is David", "The couple includes a spouse relationship.". Distinct from colleague, which indicates a professional relationship, or parent, which indicates a familial relationship.

candidates.label: isRelatedTo
candidates.comment: A general association relation between two products or services that have some unspecified connection. Also called associated with, connected to, linked to, relevant to. Examples: A smartphone isRelatedTo 'a smart watch'. A car service isRelatedTo 'car insurance'. A book isRelatedTo 'a movie adaptation'. Distinct from isSimilarTo, which implies functional similarity, and isAccessoryOrSparePartFor or isConsumableFor, which imply specific functional dependencies. This is a very general relation.

candidates.label: isPartOf
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation indicating that an item or creative work is a component of a larger creative work or resource. Also called component of, member of, contained in, element of. Examples: A chapter isPartOf 'a book'. An episode isPartOf 'a TV series'. A web page isPartOf 'a website'. Distinct from hasPart, which expresses the inverse relationship (the whole *has* a part).

candidates.label: lifeEvent
candidates.comment: A life event relation between a person and a significant event in their life. Also called: significant event, personal milestone, biographical event. Examples: "John Doe lifeEvent Baptism", "Jane Smith lifeEvent Graduation Ceremony", "Family lifeEvent Wedding".

candidates.label: isSimilarTo
candidates.comment: A functional resemblance relation between two products or services that share similar characteristics or purposes. Also called similar to, comparable to, analogous to, like. Examples: Product A isSimilarTo 'Product B' (a competitor's product). Service X isSimilarTo 'Service Y' (an alternative service). A specific brand of coffee isSimilarTo 'another brand of coffee'. Distinct from isRelatedTo, which is a more general association without implying functional similarity.

candidates.label: knows
candidates.comment: A general acquaintance relation between two people who are known to each other socially or professionally. Also called acquainted with, familiar with, knows personally, has met. Examples: John knows 'Jane'. Sarah knows 'her colleague Tom'. The CEO knows 'the board members'. Distinct from follows, friend, or memberOf, which imply more specific types of relationships.

candidates.label: relatedTo
candidates.comment: A familial relation between two people, representing a generic family connection. Also called family member, kin, relative. Examples: "John is related to 'Jane'.", "Mary is related to 'Tom'.", "Aunt Sally is related to 'Nephew Bob'."

candidates.label: isGift
candidates.comment: A transaction intent relation indicating whether an order was placed as a gift for a recipient other than the buyer. Also called gift purchase, purchased as gift, gift order. Examples: An order has isGift set to 'true'. A purchase has isGift set to 'false'. A book order has isGift set to 'true' with gift wrapping.

candidates.label: isPlanForApartment
candidates.comment: A descriptive relation between a floor plan and the accommodation unit it illustrates. Also called plan for, describes accommodation, layout for. Examples: A floor plan isPlanForApartment 'Apartment 3B'. A floor plan isPlanForApartment 'a studio apartment'. A floor plan isPlanForApartment 'Unit 101'.

candidates.label: isFamilyFriendly
candidates.comment: A content suitability relation indicating whether a creative work, offer, or product is appropriate for families. Also called family-safe, suitable for all ages, kid-friendly, appropriate for families. Examples: A movie has isFamilyFriendly set to 'true'. A video game has isFamilyFriendly set to 'false'. A restaurant offer has isFamilyFriendly set to 'true'.

relations.definition: To have a wedding ceremony or celebration at a particular location.
relations.embedding_query_text: hasWeddingAt: To have a wedding ceremony or celebration at a particular location.

chosen_property.label: location
chosen_property.justification: The location property matches the relation of having a wedding at a particular location.

candidates.label: announcementLocation
candidates.comment: An announcement location relation between a special announcement and the specific civic structure or local business it pertains to. Also called relevant location, associated place, specific venue. Examples: "A special announcement's announcement location is 'City Hall'.", "The emergency announcement's announcement location is 'Local Grocery Store'." Distinct from spatialCoverage, which is used for larger geographic regions.

candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

candidates.label: recordedAt
candidates.comment: A recording location relation between a creative work and the event where it was recorded. Also called recorded during, captured at event. Examples: "A live album was recorded at 'Wembley Stadium Concert'.", "A documentary film was recorded at 'the Amazon Rainforest Expedition'.", "A podcast episode was recorded at 'a conference panel discussion'.". Distinct from recordedIn, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: deathPlace
candidates.comment: A geographical event relation between a person and the place where they died. Also called: place of demise, passing location, decease location. Examples: "Historical Figure" death place "Dallas, Texas", "Family Member" death place "London, UK". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the place of birth.

candidates.label: hasMap
candidates.comment: A map relation between a place and its associated map or map URL. Also called map of, location map, geographical map. Examples: "A restaurant has a map of its location.", "The park has a map showing its trails.", "This place has a map URL."

candidates.label: hasParticipationOffer
candidates.comment: A participation offer relation between an event and an offer to participate in it. Also called call for participation, participation opportunity, event entry offer. Examples: "An event has a participation offer for speakers.", "The conference has a participation offer for proposals.", "This festival includes a participation offer for performers.". Distinct from hasSponsorshipOffer, which is an offer to sponsor the event.

candidates.label: legalAddress
candidates.comment: An official location relation between an organization and its legally registered postal address for administrative and tax purposes. Also called registered address, official address, corporate address, statutory address. Examples: An organization has a legalAddress of '100 Main St, Anytown, USA'. A company's legalAddress is 'Suite 200, Business Park, City'. The corporation's legalAddress is its registered office. Distinct from address, which is a general contact address, and branchOf, which is about organizational hierarchy.

candidates.label: foundingLocation
candidates.comment: A founding location relation between an organization and the place where it was established. Also called: place of origin, establishment location, birthplace. Examples: "Microsoft" founding location "Albuquerque, New Mexico", "Apple Inc." founding location "Los Altos, California", "Google" founding location "Menlo Park, California".

candidates.label: sportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A specific location relation between an exercise action and the sports activity venue where it took place. Also called "exercise location", "training venue", "athletic facility", "gym location". Examples: "The run had sportsActivityLocation Central Park", "The workout's sportsActivityLocation was the local gym", "This exercise action took place at a sportsActivityLocation stadium.". Distinct from location, which is a more general location property.

candidates.label: foodEstablishment
candidates.comment: A food establishment relation between a cook action and the specific place or food establishment where the cooking occurred. Also called: cooking location, restaurant, kitchen. Examples: "Chef prepares meal" food establishment "Gourmet Restaurant", "Home Cook makes dinner" food establishment "My Kitchen", "Baker bakes bread" food establishment "Local Bakery". Distinct from foodEvent, which is a specific event.

relations.definition: To be situated or found in a particular place or location.
relations.embedding_query_text: isLocatedIn: To be situated or found in a particular place or location.

instances: Madison Square Garden -> New York City

chosen_property.label: containedInPlace
chosen_property.justification: The containedInPlace property matches the relation of being located in a particular place.

candidates.label: isLocatedInSubcellularLocation
candidates.comment: A subcellular localization relation between a biochemical entity and its specific location within a cell. Also called found in subcellular location, localized to, present in subcellular compartment. Examples: A protein is isLocatedInSubcellularLocation 'cytoplasm'. DNA is isLocatedInSubcellularLocation 'nucleus'. Mitochondrial enzymes are isLocatedInSubcellularLocation 'mitochondrion'.

candidates.label: toLocation
candidates.comment: A destination location relation between an action (like exercise, insert, move, or transfer) and the final place of the object or agent after the action. Also called destination, final location, arrival place. Examples: "MoveAction toLocation 'New York'", "TransferAction toLocation 'Warehouse B'", "ExerciseAction toLocation 'gym'". Distinct from location, which is the general place where something is or occurs.

candidates.label: fromLocation
candidates.comment: A from location relation between an exercise, move, or transfer action and the original place of the object or agent before the action occurred. Also called: origin location, starting point, departure place. Examples: "Package Delivery" from location "Warehouse A", "Person Moving" from location "Old Apartment", "Data Transfer" from location "Server Room 1". Distinct from toLocation, which is the destination after the action.

candidates.label: homeLocation
candidates.comment: A home location relation between a person and their residential contact point or place. Also called residence, dwelling, home address. Examples: "A person has a home location in London.", "Her home location is a specific address.", "The individual's home location is a contact point."

candidates.label: contentLocation
candidates.comment: A descriptive relation for a creative work, indicating the place depicted or described within its content. Also called "depicted location", "setting", "place of content". Examples: "Photograph contentLocation 'Eiffel Tower'", "Novel contentLocation 'London'".

candidates.label: gameLocation
candidates.comment: A game location relation between a game or video game series and a real or fictional place where the game or part of it is set. Also called: game setting, virtual world, game environment. Examples: "Grand Theft Auto V" game location "Los Santos", "The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild" game location "Hyrule", "Assassin's Creed Valhalla" game location "England".

candidates.label: studyLocation
candidates.comment: A geographic relation between a medical study and the administrative area where it is conducted or was conducted. Also called "research location", "trial site", "study area", "geographic scope of study". Examples: "The medical study has studyLocation New York", "The clinical trial's studyLocation is Europe", "This study is taking place in a specific studyLocation."

candidates.label: displayLocation
candidates.comment: A display location relation between a creative work or product and the place where it can be viewed or experienced in-person. Also called "viewing location", "exhibition place", "experience venue". Examples: "Painting 'Mona Lisa' displayLocation 'Louvre Museum'", "Product 'New Car Model' displayLocation 'Dealership Showroom'", "Sculpture displayLocation 'Art Gallery'".

candidates.label: workLocation
candidates.comment: A work location relation between a person and a contact point or place, identifying where the person performs their professional duties. Also called employment location, office address, workplace. Examples: John workLocation MainOffice, Jane workLocation RemoteHome, CompanyEmployee workLocation BranchOffice. Distinct from homeLocation, which is a person's residential address.

candidates.label: itemLocation
candidates.comment: A physical location relation between an archive component and its current place, postal address, or textual description of location. Also called current location, item whereabouts, storage location, physical location. Examples: An archive component has an itemLocation of 'Shelf 3, Box 12'. An archive component has an itemLocation of 'Library Basement'. An archive component has an itemLocation of '123 Main St, Anytown'.

relations.definition: To give money or resources to a particular cause or organization.
relations.embedding_query_text: donatesTo: To give money or resources to a particular cause or organization.

instances: Taylor Swift -> Taylor Swift's Charity Donation

chosen_property.label: recipient
chosen_property.justification: The recipient property matches the relation of donating to a particular cause or organization.

candidates.label: recipient
candidates.comment: A recipient relation between an action (like sending or paying) and the audience, contact point, organization, or person receiving it. Also called receiver, intended for, sent to. Examples: "A message has a recipient 'John Doe'.", "A donation has a recipient 'Charity Organization'.", "A payment has a recipient 'Vendor Inc.'."

candidates.label: funder
candidates.comment: A funder relation between a creative work, event, grant, organization, or person and the organization or person providing financial support or sponsorship. Also called: sponsor, benefactor, financial supporter. Examples: "Art Exhibition" funder "National Endowment for the Arts", "Research Project" funder "NIH", "Charity Event" funder "Local Bank". Distinct from fundedItem, which is the item receiving funding.

candidates.label: funding
candidates.comment: A funding relation between a biochemical entity, creative work, event, medical entity, organization, person, or product and the grant that provides its direct or indirect financial support. Also called: grant received, sponsorship, financial support. Examples: "Cancer Research Project" funding "NIH Grant R01", "Local Theater Production" funding "Arts Council Grant", "Student Scholarship Program" funding "University Endowment Grant". Distinct from funder, which is the entity providing the funding.

candidates.label: sponsor
candidates.comment: A support relation between an entity (creative work, event, grant, study, organization, or person) and the person or organization providing financial or other backing. Also called "funded by", "supported by", "patron", "underwritten by". Examples: "The event has sponsor Acme Corp", "The medical study's sponsor is the NIH", "This artist has sponsor a private foundation."

candidates.label: fundedItem
candidates.comment: A funded item relation between a grant and the biochemical entity, creative work, event, medical entity, organization, person, or product that receives direct or indirect funding or sponsorship. Also called: grant recipient, sponsored item, supported entity. Examples: "Research Grant" funded item "Cancer Research Project", "Arts Grant" funded item "Local Theater Production", "Educational Grant" funded item "Student Scholarship Program". Distinct from funding, which is the grant itself.

candidates.label: nonprofitStatus
candidates.comment: The legal nonprofit status of an organization in its primary place of business. Also called charitable status, tax-exempt status, non-profit classification. Examples: "Charity A nonprofitStatus 'Nonprofit501c3'", "Foundation B nonprofitStatus 'NonprofitType.Nonprofit501c4'", "Association C nonprofitStatus 'NonprofitType.Nonprofit501c6'".

candidates.label: provider
candidates.comment: A provision relation between an action, work, program, or service and the organization or person that supplies or performs it. Also called supplied by, performed by, offered by, produced by. Examples: "A parcel delivery is provided by FedEx.", "A financial incentive is provided by the government.", "A medical service is provided by Dr. Smith."

candidates.label: offeredBy
candidates.comment: An organization or person making an offer. Also called provided by, seller, vendor, offered from. Examples: "Product Offer offeredBy 'Acme Corp'", "Service Offer offeredBy 'John Doe'", "Event Ticket Offer offeredBy 'Ticketmaster'". Distinct from seller, which is a more specific term for a person or organization selling something.

candidates.label: seeks
candidates.comment: A demand for specific products or services expressed by an organization or person. Also called desires, looks for, requests, requires. Examples: `Company X` seeks `Demand for Software Developers`, `Person Y` seeks `Demand for Used Car`, `Organization Z` seeks `Demand for Consulting Services`. Distinct from `offers`, which is about what is provided.

candidates.label: endorsee
candidates.comment: An endorsee relation between an endorse action and the person or organization being supported. Also called "supported entity", "beneficiary", "recipient of endorsement". Examples: "Endorse action endorsee 'Candidate A'", "Endorse action endorsee 'Charity B'", "Endorse action endorsee 'Product C'". Distinct from endorsers, which are the people or organizations providing the endorsement.

relations.definition: To have someone attend an event or gathering as a guest.
relations.embedding_query_text: hasGuest: To have someone attend an event or gathering as a guest.

chosen_property.label: attendee
chosen_property.justification: The attendee property matches the relation of having a guest at an event.

candidates.label: attendees
candidates.comment: A person present at an event. Also called: participants, guests, visitors. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendees 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendees 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendees 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendee, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: attendee
candidates.comment: A person or organization present at an event. Also called: participant, guest, visitor. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendee 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendee 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendee 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendees, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: additionalNumberOfGuests
candidates.comment: An additional number of guests relation between an RSVP action and the count of extra attendees beyond the invitee. Also called plus-one count, extra guests, total additional attendees. Examples: "An RSVP action's additional number of guests is '2'.", "The wedding RSVP indicates an additional number of guests of '1'."

candidates.label: hasParticipationOffer
candidates.comment: A participation offer relation between an event and an offer to participate in it. Also called call for participation, participation opportunity, event entry offer. Examples: "An event has a participation offer for speakers.", "The conference has a participation offer for proposals.", "This festival includes a participation offer for performers.". Distinct from hasSponsorshipOffer, which is an offer to sponsor the event.

candidates.label: hasSponsorshipOffer
candidates.comment: A sponsorship offer relation between an event and an offer to sponsor it. Also called sponsorship opportunity, sponsor package, call for sponsors. Examples: "An event has a sponsorship offer for corporate partners.", "The conference has a sponsorship offer with different tiers.", "This festival includes a sponsorship offer.". Distinct from hasParticipationOffer, which is an offer to participate in the event.

candidates.label: remainingAttendeeCapacity
candidates.comment: A remaining attendee capacity relation between an event and the number of available spots for attendees. Also called available seats, remaining tickets, open spots. Examples: "A concert has a remaining attendee capacity of 100.", "A workshop has a remaining attendee capacity of 5.", "A conference has a remaining attendee capacity of 500."

candidates.label: maximumAttendeeCapacity
candidates.comment: An attendee capacity relation between an event or place and the total number of individuals it can accommodate. Also called: maximum occupancy, total capacity, attendee limit. Examples: "Concert Venue maximumAttendeeCapacity 5000", "Conference Room maximumAttendeeCapacity 100", "Public Park maximumAttendeeCapacity 10000".

candidates.label: partySize
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the number of people a reservation is intended to accommodate. Also called number of guests, group size, capacity for. Examples: A restaurant reservation has a party size of four. A taxi reservation has a party size of two. A hotel booking has a party size of three.

candidates.label: maximumVirtualAttendeeCapacity
candidates.comment: A virtual attendee capacity relation between an event and the maximum number of individuals who can attend online. Also called: online capacity, virtual participant limit, streaming capacity. Examples: "Hybrid Conference maximumVirtualAttendeeCapacity 2000", "Webinar maximumVirtualAttendeeCapacity 500", "Online Class maximumVirtualAttendeeCapacity 100". Distinct from maximumPhysicalAttendeeCapacity, which refers to in-person attendees.

candidates.label: occupancy
candidates.comment: The allowed total occupancy in persons for an accommodation unit. Also called maximum occupancy, guest capacity, permitted persons. Examples: "Hotel Room occupancy 2", "Apartment occupancy 4", "Suite occupancy 6".

relations.definition: To be related or relevant to a particular topic or subject.
relations.embedding_query_text: isAbout: To be related or relevant to a particular topic or subject.

chosen_property.label: about
chosen_property.justification: The about property matches the relation of being related or relevant to a particular topic or subject.

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: isRelatedTo
candidates.comment: A general association relation between two products or services that have some unspecified connection. Also called associated with, connected to, linked to, relevant to. Examples: A smartphone isRelatedTo 'a smart watch'. A car service isRelatedTo 'car insurance'. A book isRelatedTo 'a movie adaptation'. Distinct from isSimilarTo, which implies functional similarity, and isAccessoryOrSparePartFor or isConsumableFor, which imply specific functional dependencies. This is a very general relation.

candidates.label: isAvailableGenerically
candidates.comment: A drug availability relation indicating whether a drug is available in a generic formulation. Also called generic form available, generic equivalent, generic option. Examples: A drug has isAvailableGenerically set to 'true'. A brand-name medication has isAvailableGenerically set to 'false'. A common painkiller has isAvailableGenerically set to 'true'. Distinct from isProprietary, which indicates if the *name* is proprietary.

candidates.label: isAcceptingNewPatients
candidates.comment: A patient status relation indicating whether a medical organization is currently accepting new patients. Also called accepting new patients, open to new patients, taking new patients. Examples: A clinic has isAcceptingNewPatients set to 'true'. A hospital has isAcceptingNewPatients set to 'false'. A doctor's office has isAcceptingNewPatients set to 'true'.

candidates.label: isAccessibleForFree
candidates.comment: An access cost relation indicating whether a creative work, event, or place can be accessed without charge. Also called free access, no charge, complimentary access, free of cost. Examples: A public park has isAccessibleForFree set to 'true'. An online article has isAccessibleForFree set to 'true'. A concert has isAccessibleForFree set to 'false'.

candidates.label: temporal
candidates.comment: A general temporal relation between a creative work and a date or time, used when more specific temporal properties are not applicable. Also called "related to time", "time context", "associated temporal period", "timeframe". Examples: "The novel has temporal the 19th century", "The painting's temporal is the Renaissance era", "This document's temporal is the year 2020.". Distinct from temporalCoverage, which indicates the specific time period the content applies to.

candidates.label: relevantOccupation
candidates.comment: A relevant occupation relation between a job posting and the specific occupation it describes. Also called job role, occupation type. Examples: "A job posting for 'Software Engineer' has a relevant occupation 'Software Developer'.", "A job posting for 'Nurse Practitioner' has a relevant occupation 'Registered Nurse'.", "A job posting for 'Marketing Manager' has a relevant occupation 'Marketing Professional'."

candidates.label: knowsAbout
candidates.comment: A knowledge domain relation between an organization or person and a topic or entity they possess knowledge about. Also called knowledgeable about, familiar with topic, understands, has expertise in (without implying skill level). Examples: A person knowsAbout 'artificial intelligence'. An organization knowsAbout 'renewable energy policy'. A researcher knowsAbout 'quantum physics'. Distinct from hasOccupation or alumniOf, which are about formal roles or education, not general knowledge.

candidates.label: isAccessoryOrSparePartFor
candidates.comment: A product compatibility relation between a product and the other products for which it serves as an accessory or spare part. Also called accessory for, spare part for, compatible with, used with. Examples: A phone case isAccessoryOrSparePartFor 'iPhone 15'. A replacement battery isAccessoryOrSparePartFor 'Laptop Model X'. A camera lens isAccessoryOrSparePartFor 'DSLR Camera Y'. Distinct from isConsumableFor, which refers to items that are used up.

chosen_property.label: playsFor
chosen_property.definition: To participate in a sports team or organization.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits this relation.

candidates.label: playMode
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the supported gameplay modes for a video game or series, such as single-player, multi-player, or co-op. Also called game mode, player configuration, gameplay style. Examples: A video game has a play mode of 'SinglePlayer'. A video game has a play mode of 'MultiPlayer'. A video game has a play mode of 'CoOp'.

candidates.label: validFor
candidates.comment: A valid for relation between a credential or permit and the duration of its validity. Also called duration of validity, valid period, effective duration. Examples: "Permit validFor 'P1Y'", "Credential validFor 'P5Y'", "License validFor 'P6M'".

candidates.label: isConsumableFor
candidates.comment: A product dependency relation between a product and the other products that consume it or require it for operation. Also called consumable for, used by, required by, compatible consumable. Examples: An ink cartridge isConsumableFor 'Printer Model X'. Coffee pods areConsumableFor 'Coffee Machine Y'. Batteries areConsumableFor 'Remote Control Z'. Distinct from isAccessoryOrSparePartFor, which refers to items that are not used up.

candidates.label: worksFor
candidates.comment: An employment relation between a person and an organization, indicating the organization for which the person is employed. Also called employed by, affiliated with, works at, employed at. Examples: Employee worksFor CompanyA, Consultant worksFor AgencyB, Professor worksFor UniversityC. Distinct from memberOf, which indicates general membership in a group, not necessarily employment.

candidates.label: isAccessoryOrSparePartFor
candidates.comment: A product compatibility relation between a product and the other products for which it serves as an accessory or spare part. Also called accessory for, spare part for, compatible with, used with. Examples: A phone case isAccessoryOrSparePartFor 'iPhone 15'. A replacement battery isAccessoryOrSparePartFor 'Laptop Model X'. A camera lens isAccessoryOrSparePartFor 'DSLR Camera Y'. Distinct from isConsumableFor, which refers to items that are used up.

candidates.label: reservationFor
candidates.comment: A reservation for relation between a reservation and the specific item or service being booked. Also called booked item, reserved item, subject of reservation. Examples: "A reservation is for 'Flight BA249'.", "A restaurant booking is for 'Dinner at The Fancy Bistro'.", "A hotel reservation is for 'Room 301'."

candidates.label: gameServer
candidates.comment: A game server relation between a video game and the server where it can be played. Also called: hosted on, playable server, game host. Examples: "Minecraft" game server "Hypixel Network", "World of Warcraft" game server "Frostmourne Realm", "Call of Duty" game server "Dedicated Server". Distinct from game, which is the game itself.

candidates.label: inPlaylist
candidates.comment: A playlist inclusion relation between a music recording and the music playlist it belongs to. Also called part of playlist, on playlist, playlist track. Examples: "A music recording is in a playlist titled 'Workout Mix'.", "The song is in a playlist.", "This recording belongs to a specific playlist.". Distinct from inAlbum, which refers to a music album.

candidates.label: numberOfPlayers
candidates.comment: The number of people who can play a game or video game series, often expressed as a minimum, maximum, or range. Also called player count, game capacity, participant number. Examples: "Board Game X numberOfPlayers '2-4'", "Video Game Y numberOfPlayers '1 (single-player)'", "Online Game Z numberOfPlayers '100 (max)'".

candidates.label: actor
candidates.comment: An actor relation between a creative work (e.g., movie, episode, video game) or event and a person or performing group who performs in it. Also called performer, cast member, player. Examples: "A movie's actor is 'Tom Hanks'.", "A play's actor is 'The Ensemble Theatre'.", "An episode's actor is 'Jane Doe'." Distinct from actors, which is a deprecated property for the same concept.

chosen_property.label: attendee
chosen_property.justification: The attendee property matches the relation of attending an event.

candidates.label: attendee
candidates.comment: A person or organization present at an event. Also called: participant, guest, visitor. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendee 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendee 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendee 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendees, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: attendees
candidates.comment: A person present at an event. Also called: participants, guests, visitors. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendees 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendees 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendees 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendee, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: alumniOf
candidates.comment: An alumni of relation between a person and an educational organization or organization they are a former student or member of. Also called graduated from, formerly attended, past affiliation. Examples: "A person is alumni of 'MIT'.", "John Doe is alumni of 'Boy Scouts of America'." Distinct from alumni, which describes the inverse relationship (organization to person).

candidates.label: eventAttendanceMode
candidates.comment: An event attendance mode relation between an event and the enumeration indicating whether it occurs online, offline, or a mix. Also called "attendance format", "event delivery mode", "participation mode". Examples: "Event 'Conference' eventAttendanceMode 'OnlineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Workshop' eventAttendanceMode 'OfflineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Hybrid Meeting' eventAttendanceMode 'MixedEventAttendanceMode'".

candidates.label: rsvpResponse
candidates.comment: The specific response (e.g., Yes, No, Maybe) provided to an RSVP request. Also called RSVP status, attendance response, invitation reply. Examples: `Wedding RSVP` rsvpResponse `RsvpResponseType: Yes`, `Conference RSVP` rsvpResponse `RsvpResponseType: No`, `Party Invitation` rsvpResponse `RsvpResponseType: Maybe`.

candidates.label: participant
candidates.comment: A collaborative relation between an action and an organization or person who indirectly participated in it. Also called collaborated with, involved, assisted by, co-agent. Examples: A writing action has a participant co-author. A research project has a participant researcher. A meeting has a participant attendee. Distinct from agent, which is the primary actor of an action.

candidates.label: additionalNumberOfGuests
candidates.comment: An additional number of guests relation between an RSVP action and the count of extra attendees beyond the invitee. Also called plus-one count, extra guests, total additional attendees. Examples: "An RSVP action's additional number of guests is '2'.", "The wedding RSVP indicates an additional number of guests of '1'."

candidates.label: performerIn
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between a person and an event in which they perform or participate. Also called performs in, participates in, acts in, presents at. Examples: John Doe is a performer in 'The Annual Gala'. Jane Smith is a performer in 'The City Marathon'. An actor is a performer in 'The New Play'. Distinct from performer, which points from an event to a person.

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: lifeEvent
candidates.comment: A life event relation between a person and a significant event in their life. Also called: significant event, personal milestone, biographical event. Examples: "John Doe lifeEvent Baptism", "Jane Smith lifeEvent Graduation Ceremony", "Family lifeEvent Wedding".

chosen_property.label: waitsOutside
chosen_property.definition: To wait outside a particular location or event.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits this relation.

candidates.label: checkoutTime
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a lodging business or reservation, indicating the latest time for check-out. Also called "departure time", "latest check-out", "check-out ends". Examples: "Hotel lodging business checkoutTime '11:00'", "Flight reservation checkoutTime '2023-10-27T10:00:00'". Distinct from checkinTime, which specifies the earliest time for arrival.

candidates.label: deliveryLeadTime
candidates.comment: A temporal delay relation between a demand or offer and the typical time between order receipt and goods leaving the warehouse or being ready for pickup. Also called: lead time, dispatch time, preparation time. Examples: "Product Offer" delivery lead time "2-3 business days", "Custom Order" delivery lead time "1 week", "In-store Pickup" delivery lead time "2 hours". Distinct from deliveryTime, which is the total time until the goods reach the customer.

candidates.label: arrivalBusStop
candidates.comment: An arrival bus stop relation between a bus trip and the station or stop where it concludes. Also called destination bus stop, final bus station. Examples: "A bus trip's arrival bus stop is 'Grand Central Station'.", "The bus trip's arrival bus stop is 'Main Street Stop'."

candidates.label: departureBusStop
candidates.comment: A geographical origin relation between a bus trip and the stop or station from which it departs. Also called: origin bus stop, departure bus station, bus departure point. Examples: "Bus Route 101" departure bus stop "Central Bus Station", "Intercity Bus" departure bus stop "Port Authority Bus Terminal". Distinct from arrivalBusStop, which is the destination stop.

candidates.label: departureStation
candidates.comment: A geographical origin relation between a train trip and the station from which it departs. Also called: origin train station, departure rail station, train departure point. Examples: "Train to Paris" departure station "London St Pancras International", "Commuter Train" departure station "Grand Central Terminal". Distinct from arrivalStation, which is the destination station.

candidates.label: pickupLocation
candidates.comment: A spatial attribute indicating the place where a taxi will pick up a passenger or a rental car can be collected. Also called collection point, pick-up point, embarkation point. Examples: A taxi reservation has a pickup location of 'Grand Central Station'. A rental car reservation has a pickup location of 'Airport Terminal 1'. The ride-share booking has a pickup location at 'Home Address'.

candidates.label: dropoffLocation
candidates.comment: A drop-off location relation between a rental car reservation and the place where the rental car can be returned. Also called "return location", "car return point", "drop-off point". Examples: "Rental car reservation dropoffLocation 'Airport Terminal 2'", "Car rental dropoffLocation 'Downtown Office'", "Reservation dropoffLocation 'Hotel Parking Lot'".

candidates.label: acceptsReservations
candidates.comment: A reservation acceptance status indicating whether a food establishment allows bookings. Also called takes reservations, booking available, reservation policy. Examples: "A restaurant accepts reservations is true.", "The cafe accepts reservations via its website URL.", "This diner accepts reservations is 'No'."

candidates.label: dropoffTime
candidates.comment: A drop-off time relation between a rental car reservation and the date and time when the rental car can be returned. Also called "return time", "car return time". Examples: "Rental car reservation dropoffTime '2023-10-27T10:00'", "Car rental dropoffTime '2023-11-05T17:30'".

candidates.label: checkoutPageURLTemplate
candidates.comment: A URL template for an offer, providing the structure for its checkout page. Also called "checkout URL", "purchase link template", "order page URL". Examples: "Product offer checkoutPageURLTemplate 'https://example.com/checkout{?productId,quantity}'", "Service offer checkoutPageURLTemplate 'https://shop.example.org/buy/{id}'".

chosen_property.label: isMayorOf
chosen_property.definition: To hold the office of mayor in a particular city or town.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits this relation.

candidates.label: isPartOf
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation indicating that an item or creative work is a component of a larger creative work or resource. Also called component of, member of, contained in, element of. Examples: A chapter isPartOf 'a book'. An episode isPartOf 'a TV series'. A web page isPartOf 'a website'. Distinct from hasPart, which expresses the inverse relationship (the whole *has* a part).

candidates.label: isVariantOf
candidates.comment: A product variation relation between a product or product model and the base product or product group from which it is a specific variant. Also called variant of, version of, derived from product, specific model of. Examples: A 'red iPhone 15' isVariantOf 'iPhone 15 Pro'. A 'size L t-shirt' isVariantOf 'Basic T-Shirt ProductGroup'. A 'diesel car model' isVariantOf 'Car Model X'. Distinct from isRelatedTo or isSimilarTo, as it implies a direct hierarchical relationship of variation from a base product or group.

candidates.label: increasesRiskOf
candidates.comment: A risk amplification relation between a medical risk factor and the medical entity (condition, complication) whose likelihood it increases. Also called heightens risk of, raises risk of, predisposes to, contributes to risk of. Examples: Smoking increasesRiskOf lung cancer. High blood pressure increasesRiskOf heart attack. Obesity increasesRiskOf type 2 diabetes.

candidates.label: estimatesRiskOf
candidates.comment: A risk estimation relation between a medical risk estimator and the medical entity whose risk is being assessed. Also called "predicts risk for", "assesses likelihood of", "calculates risk of". Examples: "Medical risk estimator 'Framingham Score' estimatesRiskOf 'Cardiovascular Disease'", "Genetic test estimatesRiskOf 'Type 2 Diabetes'", "Screening tool estimatesRiskOf 'Breast Cancer'".

candidates.label: isProprietary
candidates.comment: A naming status relation indicating whether a dietary supplement or drug is identified by a proprietary or brand name. Also called brand name, proprietary name, trademarked name. Examples: A drug has isProprietary set to 'true' (e.g., Tylenol). A dietary supplement has isProprietary set to 'false' (e.g., Acetaminophen). A medication has isProprietary set to 'true'. Distinct from isAvailableGenerically, which indicates if a generic *form* exists, not if the *name* itself is proprietary.

candidates.label: iswcCode
candidates.comment: A music composition identification relation between a music composition and its International Standard Musical Work Code. Also called ISWC identifier, composition code, musical work ID. Examples: A music composition has an iswcCode of 'T-034.045.001-6'. A song has an iswcCode of 'T-901.234.567-8'. A classical piece has an iswcCode of 'T-123.456.789-0'. Distinct from isrcCode, which is for music recordings, not compositions.

candidates.label: isGift
candidates.comment: A transaction intent relation indicating whether an order was placed as a gift for a recipient other than the buyer. Also called gift purchase, purchased as gift, gift order. Examples: An order has isGift set to 'true'. A purchase has isGift set to 'false'. A book order has isGift set to 'true' with gift wrapping.

candidates.label: isrcCode
candidates.comment: A music recording identification relation between a music recording and its International Standard Recording Code. Also called ISRC identifier, recording code, music track ID. Examples: A music recording has an isrcCode of 'US-S1Z-99-00001'. A song has an isrcCode of 'GB-LFB-04-00001'. An album track has an isrcCode of 'QZ-F89-12-00001'. Distinct from iswcCode, which is for musical compositions, not recordings.

candidates.label: isPartOfBioChemEntity
candidates.comment: A biochemical part-whole relation indicating that one biochemical entity is a component of another larger biochemical entity. Also called component of biochem entity, contained within biochem entity, element of biochem entity. Examples: A protein domain isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a larger protein'. A subunit isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a protein complex'. A specific gene sequence isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a chromosome'.

candidates.label: isicV4
candidates.comment: An industry classification relation between an organization, person, or place and its International Standard Industrial Classification of All Economic Activities (ISIC) Revision 4 code. Also called ISIC code, industry classification code, economic activity code. Examples: An organization has an isicV4 of '6201' (Computer programming activities). A person has an isicV4 of '8620' (Medical and dental practice activities). A place has an isicV4 of '5510' (Hotels and similar accommodation).

chosen_property.label: alumniOf
chosen_property.justification: The alumniOf property matches the relation of attending a university, but the direction is inverse.

candidates.label: attendee
candidates.comment: A person or organization present at an event. Also called: participant, guest, visitor. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendee 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendee 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendee 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendees, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: maximumAttendeeCapacity
candidates.comment: An attendee capacity relation between an event or place and the total number of individuals it can accommodate. Also called: maximum occupancy, total capacity, attendee limit. Examples: "Concert Venue maximumAttendeeCapacity 5000", "Conference Room maximumAttendeeCapacity 100", "Public Park maximumAttendeeCapacity 10000".

candidates.label: attendees
candidates.comment: A person present at an event. Also called: participants, guests, visitors. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendees 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendees 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendees 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendee, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: maximumVirtualAttendeeCapacity
candidates.comment: A virtual attendee capacity relation between an event and the maximum number of individuals who can attend online. Also called: online capacity, virtual participant limit, streaming capacity. Examples: "Hybrid Conference maximumVirtualAttendeeCapacity 2000", "Webinar maximumVirtualAttendeeCapacity 500", "Online Class maximumVirtualAttendeeCapacity 100". Distinct from maximumPhysicalAttendeeCapacity, which refers to in-person attendees.

candidates.label: maximumPhysicalAttendeeCapacity
candidates.comment: A physical attendee capacity relation between an event and the maximum number of individuals who can physically attend. Also called: in-person capacity, venue limit, on-site capacity. Examples: "Hybrid Conference maximumPhysicalAttendeeCapacity 500", "Live Concert maximumPhysicalAttendeeCapacity 10000", "Workshop maximumPhysicalAttendeeCapacity 30". Distinct from maximumVirtualAttendeeCapacity, which refers to online attendees.

candidates.label: remainingAttendeeCapacity
candidates.comment: A remaining attendee capacity relation between an event and the number of available spots for attendees. Also called available seats, remaining tickets, open spots. Examples: "A concert has a remaining attendee capacity of 100.", "A workshop has a remaining attendee capacity of 5.", "A conference has a remaining attendee capacity of 500."

candidates.label: alumniOf
candidates.comment: An alumni of relation between a person and an educational organization or organization they are a former student or member of. Also called graduated from, formerly attended, past affiliation. Examples: "A person is alumni of 'MIT'.", "John Doe is alumni of 'Boy Scouts of America'." Distinct from alumni, which describes the inverse relationship (organization to person).

candidates.label: eventAttendanceMode
candidates.comment: An event attendance mode relation between an event and the enumeration indicating whether it occurs online, offline, or a mix. Also called "attendance format", "event delivery mode", "participation mode". Examples: "Event 'Conference' eventAttendanceMode 'OnlineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Workshop' eventAttendanceMode 'OfflineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Hybrid Meeting' eventAttendanceMode 'MixedEventAttendanceMode'".

candidates.label: numberOfAccommodationUnits
candidates.comment: The total number of accommodation units in an apartment complex or for a specific floor plan. Also called total units, unit count, accommodation unit total. Examples: "Apartment Complex A numberOfAccommodationUnits 150", "Floor Plan B numberOfAccommodationUnits 10", "Building C numberOfAccommodationUnits 200". Distinct from numberOfAvailableAccommodationUnits, which specifies only the currently available units.

candidates.label: employmentUnit
candidates.comment: An employment unit relation between a job posting and the organization (department, unit, or facility) where the job is performed. Also called "department", "work unit", "reporting unit". Examples: "Job posting 'Software Engineer' employmentUnit 'Engineering Department'", "Job 'Sales Associate' employmentUnit 'Retail Store #123'", "Job 'HR Specialist' employmentUnit 'Human Resources Division'".

chosen_property.label: visitsFrom
chosen_property.definition: To visit a particular country or place from another location.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits this relation.

candidates.label: availableFrom
candidates.comment: A date and time when an item is available for pickup from a store or locker. Also called: pickup start time, ready for collection. Examples: "DeliveryEvent 'Package' availableFrom '2023-10-27T10:00:00'", "DeliveryEvent 'Order' availableFrom '2023-10-28'". Distinct from availableThrough, which specifies the end of pickup availability.

candidates.label: availableAtOrFrom
candidates.comment: A place from which an offer can be obtained. Also called: pickup location, sales point, distribution point. Examples: "Offer 'Groceries' availableAtOrFrom 'Supermarket A'", "Offer 'Concert Tickets' availableAtOrFrom 'Venue Box Office'."

candidates.label: originatesFrom
candidates.comment: A vessel from which a lymphatic structure originates or receives afferents. Also called arises from, derived from, source vessel. Examples: "Lymphatic Vessel A originatesFrom 'Capillary Bed X'", "Thoracic Duct originatesFrom 'Cisterna Chyli'", "Lymphatic Capillary originatesFrom 'Interstitial Fluid'". Distinct from runsTo, which describes the destination.

candidates.label: expectedArrivalFrom
candidates.comment: An expected arrival from relation between a parcel delivery and the earliest date or datetime the package is anticipated to arrive. Also called: earliest arrival, minimum delivery date, estimated start arrival. Examples: "Amazon Order #123" expected arrival from "2023-10-26", "UPS Package #456" expected arrival from "2023-10-27T09:00:00", "International Shipment" expected arrival from "2023-11-01". Distinct from expectedArrivalUntil, which is the latest arrival date.

candidates.label: attendee
candidates.comment: A person or organization present at an event. Also called: participant, guest, visitor. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendee 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendee 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendee 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendees, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: acquiredFrom
candidates.comment: An acquired from relation between ownership information and the organization or person from whom a product was obtained. Also called purchased from, obtained from, source of acquisition. Examples: "The car's ownership info indicates it was acquired from 'Dealership X'.", "The book's ownership info shows it was acquired from 'John Doe'."

candidates.label: sourcedFrom
candidates.comment: An anatomical origin relation between a nerve and the brain structure from which its neurons originate. Also called "originates from", "nerve pathway source", "derived from brain structure". Examples: "The optic nerve is sourcedFrom the diencephalon", "Cranial nerve V is sourcedFrom the brainstem", "This nerve's neurons are sourcedFrom the spinal cord."

candidates.label: ownedFrom
candidates.comment: The date and time when ownership of a product was obtained. Also called acquisition date, purchase date, date acquired. Examples: "Car OwnershipInfo ownedFrom '2020-01-15'", "House OwnershipInfo ownedFrom '2018-06-01T10:00:00'", "Book OwnershipInfo ownedFrom '2023-03-10'". Distinct from ownedThrough, which is the date ownership ended.

candidates.label: attendees
candidates.comment: A person present at an event. Also called: participants, guests, visitors. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendees 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendees 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendees 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendee, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: touristType
candidates.comment: A tourist type relation between a tourist attraction, destination, or trip and the specific audience or type of tourist it is suitable for. Also called target tourist, suitable for, visitor type. Examples: "TouristAttraction touristType 'children'", "TouristDestination touristType 'adventure seekers'", "TouristTrip touristType 'visitors from Japan'".

chosen_property.label: location
chosen_property.justification: The location property matches the relation of an event taking place in a particular location.

candidates.label: containedInPlace
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedInPlace 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedInPlace 'Paris'". Distinct from containedIn, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: containsPlace
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and another smaller place that it contains. Also called "includes place", "encompasses", "holds". Examples: "Country 'France' containsPlace 'Paris'", "City 'Paris' containsPlace 'Eiffel Tower'". Distinct from containedIn or containedInPlace, which are the inverse relations.

candidates.label: containedIn
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedIn 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedIn 'Paris'". Distinct from containedInPlace, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: deathPlace
candidates.comment: A geographical event relation between a person and the place where they died. Also called: place of demise, passing location, decease location. Examples: "Historical Figure" death place "Dallas, Texas", "Family Member" death place "London, UK". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the place of birth.

candidates.label: recordedIn
candidates.comment: A recording capture relation between an event and the creative work that captured all or part of it. Also called captured by, documented in, featured in. Examples: "A concert event was recorded in 'a live album'.", "A historical event was recorded in 'a documentary film'.", "A speech event was recorded in 'a news broadcast'.". Distinct from recordedAt, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: performerIn
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between a person and an event in which they perform or participate. Also called performs in, participates in, acts in, presents at. Examples: John Doe is a performer in 'The Annual Gala'. Jane Smith is a performer in 'The City Marathon'. An actor is a performer in 'The New Play'. Distinct from performer, which points from an event to a person.

candidates.label: departurePlatform
candidates.comment: An identification relation between a train trip and the platform from which it departs. Also called: platform number, train platform, departure track. Examples: "Train to Paris" departure platform "Platform 5", "Commuter Train" departure platform "Track 3". Distinct from arrivalPlatform, which is the arrival platform.

candidates.label: arrivalPlatform
candidates.comment: A platform identification for a train trip's arrival location. Also called: train arrival platform, destination platform. Examples: "TrainTrip 123 arrivalPlatform 'Platform 7'", "TrainTrip to London arrivalPlatform 'Track 1'", "TrainTrip from Paris arrivalPlatform 'Gate C'."

candidates.label: availableIn
candidates.comment: An administrative area where a drug strength is available. Also called: market availability, regional availability. Examples: "DrugStrength '500mg' availableIn 'US'", "DrugStrength '10mg' availableIn 'EU'."

candidates.label: includedInHealthInsurancePlan
candidates.comment: A health insurance plan inclusion relation between a drug and a health insurance plan that covers it. Also called covered by plan, plan coverage, drug coverage. Examples: "A drug is included in a health insurance plan.", "The medication is covered by an included in health insurance plan.", "This drug is part of a specific health insurance plan."
